discovery: Optical detection and coherent control of single electron spins in diamond, establishing solid-state spin qubits for quantum sensing and networks
motivation: Wrachtrup and Jelezko first optically detected and coherently controlled single nitrogen-vacancy spins in diamond, showing that one electron spin in a solid can be initialized, manipulated and read out optically at room temperature. They went on to demonstrate coupling to single nuclear spins and multi-qubit registers. Lukin turned this platform into a tool, proposing and demonstrating nanoscale magnetometry with single spins and spin-photon entanglement for quantum networks. Together their work created a new field. Single-defect spins now image magnetic fields in condensed-matter systems, living cells and geological samples, underpin loophole-free Bell tests and multi-node quantum networks, and have inspired a broad search for colour centres in diamond, silicon carbide and 2D materials. A single controllable quantum system in a solid has become both a window on fundamental physics and a practical quantum technology.
